config.title: Guided vs Self-Guided Berlin Walking Tour - FAQ
config.subtitle: Straight answers for choosing the first walking format on a Berlin trip.

items.q: Is a guided or self-guided Berlin walking tour better?
items.a: Neither is always better. A guided walk is stronger for first-day orientation, conversation and follow-up questions. A self-guided route is stronger for uncertain timing, private pace, frequent pauses and one narrow subject.

items.q: Should I take a guided Berlin tour on my first day?
items.a: Usually yes if the live calendar fits and you can reach the meeting point calmly. A guided first walk gives central Berlin a shape in your head, which makes later museums, neighbourhoods and self-guided routes easier to choose.

items.q: Can I do a guided and self-guided walk on the same day?
items.a: Yes, but make the second walk narrower. Use the guided walk for orientation, then follow one subject such as the Berlin Wall, socialist architecture or a museum area at your own pace. Do not repeat two broad highlight routes.

items.q: How long is the BerlinWalk free walking tour?
items.a: BerlinWalk lasts about 2 hours. It starts at the World Clock on Alexanderplatz, explores the historic centre of former East Berlin and ends at Hackescher Markt. The live calendar confirms the exact available date and time.

items.q: Does the BerlinWalk tour follow the Berlin Wall route?
items.a: No. It connects divided-city history to places in the historic centre of former East Berlin, but it does not follow the Berlin Wall line. Use the Berlin Wall Memorial at Bernauer Strasse as a separate Wall-focused visit.
